newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan capital spending gathering strength - survey.
newsitem.headline: Japan capital spending gathering strength - survey.

text.p: The recovery in Japan's corporate capital spending has increased in strength and spread to a wider range of industries, a survey by the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan (LTCB) showed on Monday.

Capital expenditure by Japanese firms is expected to rise 6.4 percent year-on-year for fiscal 1996/97 ending March 31, up 1.8 percentage points from the previous LTCB survey conducted in February. This would be the second year in a row that firms increased their capital spending plans.
Plans for 1997/98 remain cautious, with a decrease of 2.6 percent expected, the report said.

However, the report also said manufacturing firms tended to be somewhat wary about plans for next fiscal year this early on, and that upward revisions were probable. The survey was conducted in late July.
"At this stage most plans have not been fixed. It is likely that they will be gradually upgraded," an LTCB official told reporters.

The report noted the recovery last fiscal year had been concentrated in the semiconductor and paper industries, but that it had now spread to a broader range of manufacturing and non-manufacturing industries.
It also said there was an increase in investment plans targetted at strengthening competitiveness.
"Firms are slowly moving from defensive investment to more aggressive investment," the official said.
The report said manufacturers' capital spending was expected to rise 4.2 percent this business year after a 10.7 percent increase in 1995/96.

Most manufacturers showed firm capital spending plans, although overall figures were pulled lower by a 26-percent year-on-year drop in the steel industry, primarily the result of one firm's completion of a large-scale project, it said.
Competition among semiconductor firms meant downward revisions by the key industry would be relatively small, the report added.

Capital spending plans for 1996/97 for the electrical machinery sector, of which semiconductor firms are a major component, showed an increase of 3.1 percent, down 3.4 percentage points from the February survey.
LTCB's survey comprised responses from 1,708 firms, 920 of which were classified as large. Most are LTCB customers.
